text: {"question":"How does the helium abundance measurement from LBT, combined with DESI DR2 data, influence the constraints on the electron mass variation and the matter density, and what role do deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio measurements from BBN play in limiting models that attempt to resolve the Hubble tension through such variations?","reference_answer":"The LBT helium measurement, when paired with DESI DR2, breaks the geometric degeneracy introduced by an early‑time electron‑mass shift, tightening the allowed range of the matter density Ωm and leaving the Hubble constant h less affected. Meanwhile, deuterium‑to‑hydrogen ratio constraints from BBN impose upper limits on Ωbh², which can conflict with the higher values preferred by models that reduce the Hubble tension via electron‑mass or gravitational‑coupling variations.","passage_1_contribution":"LBT’s helium measurement combined with DESI DR2 data breaks the geometric degeneracy caused by an early‑time shift in the electron mass, tightening constraints on Ωm.","passage_2_contribution":"BBN deuterium‑to‑hydrogen ratio measurements constrain Ωbh², potentially conflicting with models that use electron‑mass or gravitational‑coupling variations to ease the Hubble tension.","joint_reason":"Both passages discuss how independent observational constraints (helium abundance from LBT and deuterium ratios from BBN) limit cosmological models that modify early‑time physics to address the Hubble tension, each providing a different but complementary restriction on the parameter space.","same_quantity":false}
